exposure: previous history of mid-trimester pregnancy loss (MTL)
previous cervical trauma (loop electrosurgical excision procedure or Cesarean section in labor)
endocrine disorders (thyroid disease, polycystic ovary syndrome)
outcome: management of threatened and confirmed mid-trimester pregnancy loss
optimized outcomes for women and families
cohort: The guideline focuses on women experiencing pregnancy loss between 14 + 0 and 21 + 6 weeks of gestation, with applicability extending to births up to 28 weeks or babies weighing less than 1 kg in low-resource settings.
finding: The guideline emphasizes the importance of early assessment, accurate diagnosis, personalized, multidisciplinary care, and comprehensive psychosocial support for women experiencing mid-trimester pregnancy loss to optimize outcomes and address physical and emotional well-being.
mod_finding: Previous Cesarean section in labor is identified as a risk factor for mid-trimester pregnancy loss due to cervical trauma, and medical induction of labor or surgical intervention (dilation and evacuation) are presented as care options for confirmed loss.
gest_age: between 14 + 0 and 21 + 6 weeks of gestation (with applicability up to 28 weeks in low-resource settings)
